components.name: Station Dial
components.description: Signature: 60 bar indices (white majors, graphite minors) with the red signal disc parked at twelve while latched. Hover shows the release: the disc swings 110 degrees clockwise and fades.
components.css: .ds-dial-wrap { background: #0B0D10; padding: 24px; display: flex; justify-content: center; } .ds-dial { position: relative; width: 220px; height: 220px; } .ds-dial::before, .ds-dial::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-dial::before { background: repeating-conic-gradient(from -0.5deg, #8A8F98 0deg 1deg, transparent 1deg 6deg); -webkit-mask: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 89%, #000 89.5%, #000 96%, transparent 96.5%); mask: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 89%, #000 89.5%, #000 96%, transparent 96.5%); } .ds-dial::after { background: repeating-conic-gradient(from -1.5deg, #F2F2EE 0deg 3deg, transparent 3deg 30deg); -webkit-mask: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 76%, #000 76.5%, #000 96%, transparent 96.5%); mask: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 76%, #000 76.5%, #000 96%, transparent 96.5%); } .ds-signal { position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 1; transition: transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.2, 0.64, 1), opacity 0.5s ease-out; } .ds-signal span { position: absolute; background: #E1251B; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); } .ds-stem { top: 17.5%; height: 45%; width: 1.25%; } .ds-disc { top: 15%; width: 12%; height: 12%; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-hub { top: 48%; width: 4%; height: 4%; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-dial:hover .ds-signal { transform: rotate(110deg); opacity: 0; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-signal { transition: opacity 0.2s ease-out; } .ds-dial:hover .ds-signal { transform: none; opacity: 0; } }

components.css: .ds-list-wrap { background: #0B0D10; padding: 16px 20px; font: 400 17px/22px -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; color: #F2F2EE; } .ds-list-head { margin: 0 16px 8px; color: #8A8F98; font-size: 15px; } .ds-list { background: #1C1C1E; border-radius: 26px; margin-bottom: 20px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-row { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 14px 20px; border: none; background: none; color: inherit; font: inherit; text-align: left; } .ds-row + .ds-row { border-top: 0.5px solid rgba(84,84,88,0.65); } .ds-val { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-destructive { color: #FF453A; cursor: pointer; } .ds-destructive:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.04); } .ds-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F2F2EE; outline-offset: -2px; }

narrative.overview:
Wakelatch is a Swiss railway clock in a dark room. The red second hand on those clocks pauses at twelve and waits for the signal before it moves on. Wakelatch is that pause: a latched alarm keeps ringing until the user gives the signal by solving the challenge, and then the red disc swings away. Everything else on screen is the clock's enamel, its white bar indices and its graphite minor marks.

The app is dark-only. Both scenes it serves happen in a dark room: setting tomorrow's rings at night, and solving the challenge in the morning with bleary eyes and one hand. Screens are sparse and high-contrast: white on near-black, one dial, one sentence, one action pinned to the bottom. Native SwiftUI structure (NavigationStack, inset grouped lists, system toolbars, the system number pad) carries the app; the world lives in the colours, the dial and the single slab button. The direction refuses sunrise gradients, neon-on-black and the stock alarm list.

The world is flat. There are no custom shadows or gradients; depth comes from the system's own grouped-list and toolbar materials, and from the white slab sitting on enamel.
keyCharacteristics: One recurring form: the bar-index station dial, at every size.
Signal red means "latched" and nothing else.
SF Pro at Dynamic Type text styles, tabular digits everywhere a number appears.
One radius (12pt) and one button style (slab).
The primary action is pinned in the bottom safe-area inset.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal red means "latched" and nothing else. If the latch is not holding, no red is on screen. It is never used for text.

rules.name: The Destructive Exception Rule
rules.body: Destructive buttons ("Cancel chain", "Clear log") keep the system red that `role: .destructive` gives them. This is a deliberate exception to the Signal Rule, following the HIG convention that destructive actions are shown in the system red. Do not restyle them in signal red, and do not use the system red anywhere else.

rules.name: The Quiet Error Rule
rules.body: Errors are shown in clock-face white with an SF Symbol (`exclamationmark.triangle`), at footnote size. Never in red.

rules.name: The Dark Room Rule
rules.body: The app is dark-only (`.preferredColorScheme(.dark)` at the root and on the challenge cover). Both use scenes happen in a dark room. Do not add a light appearance.

rules.name: The Timetable Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change (times, ring counts, problems, answers, log timestamps) uses tabular digits, so values never jitter as they update.

rules.name: The Text Style Rule
rules.body: Type is set only with Dynamic Type text styles (weight may change; size may not be fixed). No custom fonts, no fixed point sizes.

rules.name: The Pinned Action Rule
rules.body: Each screen has at most one slab, and it lives in the bottom safe-area inset with a soft scroll edge behind it.

rules.name: The Fits Above the Keys Rule
rules.body: At any Dynamic Type size, the morning challenge must show its whole task above the number pad. Shrink the dial before anything else.

rules.name: The Enamel Rule
rules.body: Custom surfaces are enamel, clock white, or clock white at a stated opacity. No shadows, no gradients.

dos: Do keep every screen dark: enamel ground, `.preferredColorScheme(.dark)`.
Do reserve signal red for the latched state: the disc and the ring sounding under the latch.
Do show errors in clock-face white with an SF Symbol.
Do leave destructive buttons in the system red of `role: .destructive`, per the HIG.
Do set all type with Dynamic Type text styles and give every changing number tabular digits.
Do pin the one primary action in a bottom safe-area inset with a soft scroll-edge effect.
Do use the slab for the primary action and system button styles, tinted clock white, for everything else.
Do use the 12pt radius on any new custom rounded surface.
Do make the station dial the visual centre of any screen about the latch, and shrink it (140pt) at accessibility sizes before dropping content.
Do pair the release with the success haptic and give it a crossfade under Reduce Motion.
donts: Don't use signal red for text, errors, buttons, badges or decoration.
Don't add a second custom button style or a second radius.
Don't fix font sizes or bring in a custom typeface.
Don't add shadows or gradients; the world refuses sunrise gradients and neon-on-black.
Don't replace the dial with the stock alarm list.
Don't put the primary action inside scrolling content.
